errors-testing.summary: Know exactly how try/except/else/finally behave, how exceptions chain and group, how logging decides what to emit, and how pytest and unittest.mock work so tests catch real bugs instead of hiding them.
points: `except Exception` misses BaseException subclasses (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, GeneratorExit); a bare `except:` catches them all, which can swallow sys.exit() and Ctrl+C.
`finally` always runs. A `return` or exception inside it replaces the pending result or exception, so keep cleanup code simple and never return from it.
`raise X from e` sets __cause__ ("direct cause"), implicit raising sets __context__ ("During handling…"), and `from None` hides the context while still storing it.
`except*` (3.11+) can run several clauses for one ExceptionGroup, always binds a group, re-raises unmatched leaves as a new group, and forbids return/break/continue inside the block.
Logging: records pass the logger level, then each handler level, then propagate to ancestor handlers. basicConfig is ignored once handlers exist unless force=True. Use lazy %-style arguments.
pytest: fixtures with yield give setup/teardown, scopes control lifetime, parametrize multiplies, raises(match=) is a regex search, and approx compares floats.
unittest.mock: patch where the name is looked up, prefer spec/autospec, and remember side_effect beats return_value and raises StopIteration when an iterable runs out.
traps: The name bound by `except ... as e` is deleted when the block ends, even if `e` existed before.
`assert` statements disappear under `python -O`, so never use them for validation.
Patching `module.attr` does nothing for code that already did `from module import attr`; patch the importing module instead.
